title: Contraction of two trace maps through tensor actions
statement:
Let $\mathcal C_X,\mathcal C_Y,\mathcal C_Z$ be monoidal categories [def-sfb-monoidal-category]. Let $F_f:\mathcal C_X\to\mathcal C_Y$, $F_g:\mathcal C_Y\to\mathcal C_Z$ be functors and $P_f:\mathcal C_Y\to\mathcal C_X$, $P_g:\mathcal C_Z\to\mathcal C_Y$ strong monoidal functors [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor]. Write $\delta_{f;N,N'}:P_f(N\otimes N')\xrightarrow{\sim}P_fN\otimes P_fN'$ for the inverse tensor comparison, $\alpha$ for tensor associators, and $\lambda:\mathbf1\otimes B\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ for left unitors. For $u=f,g$ suppose given natural isomorphisms
$$\operatorname{PF}_{u;M,N}:F_uM\otimes N\xrightarrow{\sim}F_u(M\otimes P_uN),\qquad q_{u;M,N}=\operatorname{PF}_{u;M,N}^{-1}.$$
The maps need only be given on full domains closed under every object, arrow and structural comparison displayed here; each equality below is restricted to those domains. Assume the tensor-action equation for $f$:
$$\operatorname{PF}_{f;M,N\otimes N'}=
F_f\bigl((1_M\otimes\delta_{f;N,N'}^{-1})\alpha_{M,P_fN,P_fN'}\bigr)
\operatorname{PF}_{f;M\otimes P_fN,N'}(\operatorname{PF}_{f;M,N}\otimes1_{N'})
\alpha_{F_fM,N,N'}^{-1}.$$
Composition is written right to left.

Choose objects $L_f\in\mathcal C_X$, $L_g\in\mathcal C_Y$ and arbitrary morphisms $t_f:F_fL_f\to\mathbf1_Y$, $t_g:F_gL_g\to\mathbf1_Z$. Define, for every permitted $B$,
$$d_{u,B}=\lambda_B(t_u\otimes1_B)q_{u;L_u,B}:F_u(L_u\otimes P_uB)\to B.$$
Put $L=L_f\otimes P_fL_g$, $a=d_{f,L_g}:F_fL\to L_g$ and $b=t_gF_g(a):F_gF_fL\to\mathbf1_Z$. For $K\in\mathcal C_Z$ set
$$\sigma_K=\alpha_{L_f,P_fL_g,P_fP_gK}^{-1}(1_{L_f}\otimes\delta_{f;L_g,P_gK}):
L_f\otimes P_f(L_g\otimes P_gK)\xrightarrow{\sim}L\otimes P_fP_gK.$$
Then the following equality holds as morphisms from $F_gF_f(L_f\otimes P_f(L_g\otimes P_gK))$ to $K$:
$$d_{g,K}F_g(d_{f,L_g\otimes P_gK})=
\lambda_K(b\otimes1_K)q_{g;F_fL,K}F_g(q_{f;L,P_gK})F_gF_f(\sigma_K).$$
No adjunction or comparison between $F_gF_f$ and a third functor is assumed.

proof.text:
Write $A=F_fL_f$, $B=L_g$, and $C=P_gK$, so $L=L_f\otimes P_fB$. All compositions below are right to left. The specified map $\sigma_K$ has inverse $(1_{L_f}\otimes\delta_{f;B,C}^{-1})\alpha_{L_f,P_fB,P_fC}$. Substitute $M=L_f$, $N=B$, $N'=C$ into the assumed tensor-action equation and take inverses. Since functors preserve inverse arrows and the tensor is a bifunctor, this gives the explicitly typed equality
$$q_{f;L_f,B\otimes C}=\alpha_{A,B,C}(q_{f;L_f,B}\otimes1_C)q_{f;L,C}F_f(\sigma_K).$$
Both sides go from $F_f(L_f\otimes P_f(B\otimes C))$ to $A\otimes(B\otimes C)$. This uses the tensor-action equation only at the displayed triple.

source.place: Final sentence, canonical reassociations; agent expansion: inverse of the assumed tensor-action equation.

proof.text:
Associator naturality, with the arbitrary morphism $t_f:A\to\mathbf1_Y$, gives
$$(t_f\otimes1_{B\otimes C})\alpha_{A,B,C}=\alpha_{\mathbf1_Y,B,C}((t_f\otimes1_B)\otimes1_C).$$
Apply [lem-coef-monoidal-structural-coherence] to the two formal structural arrows from $(\mathbf1_Y\otimes B)\otimes C$ to $B\otimes C$: one is $\lambda_{B\otimes C}\alpha_{\mathbf1_Y,B,C}$, the other is $\lambda_B\otimes1_C$. Their formal endpoints agree, so
$$\lambda_{B\otimes C}\alpha_{\mathbf1_Y,B,C}=\lambda_B\otimes1_C.$$
Combining these two equalities and bifunctoriality yields
$$\lambda_{B\otimes C}(t_f\otimes1_{B\otimes C})\alpha_{A,B,C}=(\lambda_B(t_f\otimes1_B))\otimes1_C.$$
Coherence is applied only to structural arrows; $t_f$ is moved using naturality, not treated as a structural generator.

proof.text:
Postcompose the equality in Step 1 with $\lambda_{B\otimes C}(t_f\otimes1_{B\otimes C})$ and use Step 2. By the definitions in the statement, $a=\lambda_B(t_f\otimes1_B)q_{f;L_f,B}$. Tensor bifunctoriality combines these factors, giving
$$d_{f,B\otimes C}=(a\otimes1_C)q_{f;L,C}F_f(\sigma_K).$$
The domain is $F_f(L_f\otimes P_f(B\otimes C))$ and the codomain is $B\otimes C$. The arrow $q_{f;L,C}$ has target $F_fL\otimes C$, so it is precisely the specified arrow to which $a\otimes1_C$ can be applied.

source.place: Final sentence, canonical reassociations; agent expansion: contraction of the first trace after the inverse action.

proof.text:
The inverse of a natural isomorphism is natural: multiply the naturality square for $\operatorname{PF}_g$ by its component inverses. At $a:F_fL\to B$ and the fixed object $K$ this says
$$q_{g;B,K}F_g(a\otimes1_{P_gK})=(F_g(a)\otimes1_K)q_{g;F_fL,K}.$$
Both sides have domain $F_g(F_fL\otimes P_gK)$ and codomain $F_gB\otimes K$. This square uses only the assumed naturality of $\operatorname{PF}_g$; no tensor-action equation for $g$ is required.

source.place: Final sentence, canonical reassociations; agent expansion: the given projection naturality in the coefficient object.

proof.text:
Apply $F_g$ to Step 3, using preservation of composition, and postcompose with $d_{g,K}=\lambda_K(t_g\otimes1_K)q_{g;B,K}$. Step 4 and tensor bifunctoriality give
$$\begin{aligned}
d_{g,K}F_g(d_{f,B\otimes C})
&=\lambda_K(t_g\otimes1_K)q_{g;B,K}F_g(a\otimes1_C)F_g(q_{f;L,C})F_gF_f(\sigma_K)\\
&=\lambda_K((t_gF_g(a))\otimes1_K)q_{g;F_fL,K}F_g(q_{f;L,C})F_gF_f(\sigma_K).
\end{aligned}$$
Insert $b=t_gF_g(a)$, $B=L_g$ and $C=P_gK$. This is exactly the asserted equality from $F_gF_f(L_f\otimes P_f(L_g\otimes P_gK))$ to $K$. Every object and arrow used is among the displayed ones or their structural comparisons, so the assumed domain-closure condition permits every substitution.
